observations: Photo 0: A DSLR camera body sitting in front of a worn cardboard box. Both the camera's top plate and the box clearly show the word 'Nikon' and the model 'D7100'.
Photo 1: The same camera held in a hand, lens mount open (no lens attached), body cap and rear cap visible nearby. The box behind it again reads 'Nikon D7100'.
No batteries are visible in either photo.
No silicone case is visible in either photo.
No Canon branding appears anywhere in the two photos.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 both show 'Nikon' and 'D7100' printed on the camera body and box, not Canon.

claims.claim: The camera is working perfectly fine
claims.evidence: No power-on, sensor, shutter-fire, or lens-mount test shown; lens mount in photo 1 is empty so no image-quality or autofocus check possible.
No batteries visible in either photo.
No case visible in either photo.

risks.risk: Brand/model misstated by seller (claims Canon, photos show Nikon D7100) — could indicate a copy-pasted or mismatched listing, or an attempt to pass off a cheaper/older body as something else.
risks.proof: A fresh photo of the actual camera top plate and lens mount together with a video showing the seller naming the correct brand/model on camera.
risks.if_unproven: Treated as a high-risk, possibly fraudulent listing; not priced as a working Canon camera.

risks.risk: Sensor/shutter functionality unknown — DSLR shown with no lens, cap off, could have mirror or shutter fault.
risks.proof: Video of camera powering on, shutter firing, and a test photo on its screen or card.

risks.risk: Included accessories (batteries, case) not shown — may not actually be included.
risks.proof: Photo of the 2 batteries and silicone case laid out next to the camera.

risks.risk: No lens included — box and photos show only a body, lens mount empty.
risks.proof: Photo confirming whether a lens is part of the sale.

proof_requests: Photo of the camera's brand label and model number matching the seller's claim of 'Canon'.
Video of the camera powering on and firing the shutter.
Photo showing the 2 batteries and silicone case alongside the camera.
Confirmation of whether a lens is included.
response.reason: The seller claims the item is a Canon, but both photos clearly show a Nikon D7100 body and matching box, a direct and significant brand contradiction that undermines trust in the rest of the listing.
